subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: From which chamber does oxygenated blood leave the heart into the aorta?
questions.explain: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta to the body.
Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds and transports oxygen.

questions.q: Lipase digests lipids (fats) into which products?
questions.explain: Lipase breaks lipids down into fatty acids and glycerol.

questions.q: The movement of sugars through phloem is called...
questions.explain: Translocation is the transport of dissolved food (sucrose) in the phloem.

questions.q: How are villi adapted for absorption?
options: No blood supply to slow diffusion
Large surface area and thin walls with good blood supply
questions.explain: Villi give a large surface area, have thin walls and a rich blood supply for efficient absorption.

questions.q: What happens to chest volume and pressure during inhalation?
options: Volume increases, pressure decreases so air flows in
questions.explain: The chest volume increases, lowering the pressure inside so air is drawn into the lungs.

questions.q: Why does increasing temperature usually increase transpiration?
options: Water molecules evaporate and diffuse faster
questions.explain: Higher temperatures speed up evaporation and diffusion of water vapour from the leaf.

questions.q: In the reflex arc, what is the 'effector'?
options: The receptor that detects the stimulus
A muscle or gland that produces the response
The relay neurone in the spinal cord
questions.explain: An effector is a muscle or gland that carries out the response, such as a muscle contracting.

questions.q: Which large vein returns deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart?
questions.explain: The vena cava carries deoxygenated blood from the body back into the right atrium.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes phloem from xylem?
options: Phloem is made of living cells
Phloem is made of dead cells
questions.explain: Phloem is composed of living cells, unlike the dead xylem vessels.

questions.q: Why do gas-exchange surfaces such as alveoli need a good blood supply?
options: To maintain steep concentration gradients for diffusion
questions.explain: A good blood supply quickly removes diffused gases, keeping a steep concentration gradient.

questions.q: Which statement about bile is correct?
options: It is made in the pancreas
It emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid
It is an enzyme that digests fat
It breaks protein into amino acids
questions.explain: Bile is not an enzyme; it emulsifies fat and is alkaline so it neutralises acid from the stomach.
